key_insight: A hybrid quantum-classical pipeline, qReduMIS, uses QAOA measurements to prune and simplify portfolio-selection graphs before classical optimization, improving solution quality and scalability.
engineering_relevance: The work shows a practical near-term quantum workflow for financial optimization, demonstrating hardware runs on a 98-qubit trapped-ion system with performance gains over standalone QAOA.
method: Formulate portfolio diversification as a Maximum Independent Set problem on asset-correlation graphs.
Use QAOA to measure candidate independent sets and identify frozen nodes.
Apply provably optimal classical reductions recursively on the reduced graph (qReduMIS).
evidence_signal: On real market data from four indices up to 225 assets, qReduMIS reached success probabilities of 0.40 and 0.95 on the two largest cases and achieved average approximation ratios of at least 0.96, with emulator tests showing a 3.2× smaller optimal time-to-solution scaling exponent than standalone QAOA for p=2.
watch_item: The approach depends on QAOA-generated freeze decisions and hardware/emulator performance, so benefits may vary with noise, graph structure, and circuit depth.
paper_title: Quantum-Informed Portfolio Selection: An End-to-End Pipeline Validated on Trapped-Ion Hardware with Real Market Data
